voice_script: [curious] Imagine you're running the chipmaker, and a huge AI IPO lands, but instead of reassuring investors, it makes them question the AI buildout. That question exposes a $3.8 trillion bet: can future AI profits justify today's spending? After Anthropic's strong debut on November 19, its shares fell on November 20, and the Nasdaq erased all its 2026 gains. That didn't prove AI failed; it changed what investors were asking. [serious] So investors started looking at the bill: data centers, chips and debt cost money now, but profits may arrive later. And that bill gets enormous: Morgan Stanley estimates hyperscalers could spend $3.8 trillion from 2026 through 2028, with more than half likely financed through credit. So when investors doubt the timing, AI-linked shares fall together, leaving the chipmaker exposed because its chips sit at the center of that buildout. And that pressure reaches people: retirement funds move, startups face tighter funding, and AI jobs must show results. [confidently] But the twist is that more efficient AI could make services cheaper. Follow the channel; the free guide and our community link are in the description. AI isn't over; the easy money story is.
